pitch_detail.notes: Initial west rib pitches with good granite and vertical jointing providing solid protection. Loose blocks in approach gully; careful foot placement required.
Upper pitches to summit with steeper, more exposed climbing. Coarse granite with vertical jointing provides adequate protection. Quality varies; test holds. Final pitches near summit.

before.beta: The North Ridge - West Side is one of the primary technical routes on Molar Tooth. The route ascends via the west rib with multiple short 5th class pitches (5.4-5.8), solid granite with vertical jointing providing good protection opportunities, and enjoyable alpine climbing despite loose rock concerns. The descent via north ridge rappels requires careful anchor placement and rope management due to potential loose rock.
before.pro_needs: Natural rock protection via cracks and vertical jointing. Granite features provide ample protection opportunities. Test all anchors before committing weight and avoid placing protection in weathered sections. Most parties find good solid placements throughout the climb.
before.detailed_rack: Bring complete trad rack with cams 0.5-3 inches, stoppers/nuts, and hexes. Vertical granite jointing provides excellent protection throughout technical pitches. Consider extra quickdraws (10-12 total) and locking carabiners for belays. Multiple moderate-length pitches with good crack systems allow solid piece placement.
